label: rem:mass-comparison-table
title: Mass predictions from knot formulas vs. CODATA/PDG values
html:
This table evaluates the topological knot formulas (knot formula table) at the substrate parameter q_0 = 1.109978582751 (anchored numerically on the proton-to-electron mass ratio m_{\mathfrak{p}}/m_e; see Skein mass relation). The results are compared against CODATA 2022 recommended values and PDG 2024 averages. All masses are in MeV/c^2.

Input parameters (one dimensionless deformation parameter q_0):

  q = q_0, \quad
  \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} \approx 0.099082, \quad
  \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2.029883.

Table 2: Predicted vs.\ observed masses.

Leptons (from Skein volume).

See Table 1.

The electron mass is a physical scale input fixing the MeV energy unit. At the proton-pinned q_0, the topological volume ratio m_e\,\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_{q_0}^2 \approx 105.658398\;\text{MeV} agrees with m_\mu to six significant figures in MeV (residual +211.2\;\text{ppb}, or 9.70\sigma against the sub-ppb CODATA uncertainty).

Hadrons (from pair Skein masses).

The proton and neutron rows derive from the LO \rho_K assembly. This assembly consumes m_p and m_n as CODATA inputs. It is tautological by construction. The |\mathrm{tr}_M| factor cancels in \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}} \cdot m_e \cdot |\mathrm{tr}_M|, reducing the output to Z m_p + N m_n. The FULL framework prediction requires the unified knot mass formula M(\mathfrak{H}) = \rho \cdot [|\mathrm{tr}_M(T_w)| + \mathrm{tower}(T_w) + \mathrm{tr}_M(C_{\dim_q})]. This formula does not yet extend to the nucleon scale. The n–p splitting emerges as a consequence of the FULL \mathfrak{Q}_\beta chain (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta + m_e \approx 0.8364\;\text{MeV} on the scored T^3 weight-trace split at z = q_0^3/(q_0^2+1), or 0.9601\;\text{MeV} on the historical \Delta base, against CODATA 1.2933\;\text{MeV}).

See Table 2.

† Tautological under the LO chain. The proton, neutron, and n-p split rows return the CODATA inputs because the LO formula collapses to Z m_p + N m_n (no binding correction).

FULL \mathfrak{Q}_\beta prediction (framework, no CODATA mass injection)

Per Symbolic Q-value of free neutron decay, the framework evaluates the \beta-decay Q-value from the electron scale m_e and proton-anchored q_0 alone:

\boxed{
\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\Delta} = \Bigl|\tfrac{h^2}{2} - h\,z\Bigr|\,\frac{m_e}{q_0(q_0-1)(1-\hbar_q^2)} \approx 0.4491 \text{ MeV}
}

with h = q_0 - q_0^{-1}, \hbar_q = 1 - q_0^{-1}, and z = q_0^3/(q_0^2+1) \approx 0.612688. Using the tower-summed E_0 (the order-zero form m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) gives 0.4447 MeV), this Markov-trace \Delta evaluation sits at -42.59\% (-333.2 keV) relative to CODATA 0.7823 MeV; no c_k correction ladder at z = q^3/(q^2+1) has yet been derived, and a cosine factor cannot exceed 1 (cos-resummation).

The scored evaluation applies the T^3 weight split of the z = q_0^3/(q_0^2+1) trace to the \gamma\gamma base V^3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3, giving \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{scored}} = |\varepsilon_{\mathrm{flavour}}(V^3)|\,E_0 \approx 0.3254 MeV (-58.40\%) and \mathfrak{m}_n - \mathfrak{m}_p \approx 0.8364 MeV (-35.33\%). On the \Delta evaluation above (0.4491 MeV), \mathfrak{m}_n - \mathfrak{m}_p = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta + m_e \approx 0.9601 MeV (-25.77\% relative to CODATA 1.2933 MeV).

Coordinate-sum Form A (z = 1 comparison). Evaluating \varepsilon at z = 1 gives m_e\,|q_0^2 - 2q_0 - 1|\,(q_0 + 1)/(2 q_0^3) \approx 0.7836 MeV (+0.168\%, m_n - m_p \approx 1.295 MeV); because z = 1 does not satisfy y_{(1^3)}(z) = 0, it serves only as an algebraic comparison.

Light nuclei (from multi-body Skein).

All rows below come from the LO \rho_K assembly using CODATA m_p, m_n inputs. The \Delta column equals the CODATA binding energy by construction. The FULL multi-body unified knot mass formula at H_{3A} remains intractable beyond A = 1. Binding-energy predictions require resolving the open \Delta_\lambda research question (see Recomputed low-isotope mass table).

See Table 3.

† LO output is constituent sum only. The full prediction (beyond the constituent sum) is not yet available.

Notes. The proton--electron mass ratio fixes the substrate parameter q_0. Hadronic masses follow from the pair Skein formula once the two dressed quark masses are given; that map is invertible, so the formula alone does not predict them (nucleon masses under the pair Skein formula). Nuclear binding follows from the Hopf-junction Skein change \Delta E = \Delta\mathcal{S}. Evaluate the multi-body Skein polynomials up to {}^4\mathrm{He}. Polynomials beyond A = 4 are computable in principle (embeddability closure) but remain unevaluated.

Sources and scope. The proton and neutron entries use CODATA 2022 values directly. The nuclear entries use AME2020 binding energies. These entries recombine observed constants. The parameter q predicts mass ratios (m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2), Q-values (\Delta\mathrm{net} \times E_0), and half-life ratios via \log_q(ft) spectroscopy. The single external scaling ruler is m_e = 0.510999\;\text{MeV} (CODATA 2022 input). This ruler converts dimensionless q-ratios to physical MeV.

Isotope-level data (hecke-engine certificates, A \leq 14).

The hecke-engine provides exact Skein polynomial evaluations at q_0 for 47 isotopes from {}^2\mathrm{H} through {}^{60}\mathrm{Co}. All 47 isotopes have corresponding AME2020 binding-energy data. The certificate fields encode combinatorial crossing structure, not mass directly.

See Table 4.

The F_{\mathrm{Pauli}} factor remains O(1) across all isotopes and encodes the Pauli exclusion statistical weight. The \ln|P| column records the transfer matrix Skein polynomial evaluated at q_0. Neither field maps linearly to B/A or mass in MeV.
